Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We loved the latency guarantees on the mid-sequence routing, and Quantix is comfortable moving forward with a dedicated pool if we can nail down two operational pieces before legal signs the term sheet:

1) Clear thresholds for when requests move out of the reserved pool into the spare pool (and vice versa).
2) How short-lived spikes are credited / debited against our quarterly cushion, and the time window used for invoicing adjustments.

A couple specifics from our side: our peak production has short spikes (~10–20 minutes) when a pipeline kick runs across 200k requests; we expect 95th P50 latency to matter more than sustained throughput. We're proposing 40 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs + a 15-GPU spare band for short spikes. Can you confirm whether that configuration will be treated as 'soft' capacity (auto-evictable) and how the auto-scale gate behaves?

I'm attaching a rough capacity table — can your ops team propose a formal gating rule we can include in the SOW? Also cc'ing ops for any immediate notes.

Appreciate it,
Jordan

Naomi / team —

Quick technical proposal for the gating rules that aligns with Quantix's burst profile:

1) Promotion threshold (reserved -> spare): when 95th-percentile token processing backlog across the customer's queue exceeds 60% of the reserved pool's sustained capacity for a rolling 6-minute window, allow allocation from the spare band up to the configured spare limit (15 GPUs).

2) Demotion / eviction: if the customer's 95th-percentile backlog drops below 35% of reserved capacity for a continuous 10-minute window, progressively release spare GPUs (evict oldest allocations first) over a 5-minute grace period.

3) Micro-ephemeral slab (for 10–30 minute spikes): allow up to 5 additional GPUs without changing commit tier. These are metered as "micro-burst" and reconciled at quarter-end. If micro-bursts exceed 300 GPU-minutes per day aggregated, they draw from the spare band's monthly cap.

4) Spin-up latency: we assume a warm-start path for spare GPUs with median attach time ~75s and 95th ~220s. For critical low-latency routes we recommend configuring a fallback model variant (quantized smaller model) to keep percentiles intact while spare GPUs spin-up.

5) Cost & crediting model: micro-burst usage is tracked per-minute and credited against a quarterly buffer of GPU-minutes. For excess sustained consumption (over 72 hours continuous above reserved), billing reclassifies to temporary overage rates per the term sheet.

Ben — can you confirm operational limits (preemption policy + visibility in console) so we can put exact wording in the SOW and invoice template?

—Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Naomi / all —

Operational confirmation and polish for Karthik's items:

- Preemption: spare-band allocations are preemptible with 10-minute notice where possible; immediate preemption is also supported for urgent reclaim but we will avoid live termination of in-flight requests by draining (5–15s drain depending on model).
- Console visibility: Quantix will see a dedicated "Spare band" telemetry pane with real-time allocation, per-route token burn and a 1, 6, 60 minute backlog heatmap.
- Alerts & runbook: we will create two alert tiers — Advisory (when spare band >50% used for 6 minutes) and Critical (when spare band >90% used and no eviction candidate). Advisory triggers account team notification; Critical triggers on-call and a recommended temporary throttle to the lowest-priority route.
